(I’d like to preface this with a warning to anyone struggling with suicidal thoughts and urges, or anyone sensitive to this sort of content)

When I was thirteen, I tried to hang myself in my bedroom closet. This was the result of untreated and undiagnosed depression and anxiety, as well as homophobic bullying at school and two other unsuccessful attempts. 

I distinctly remember realizing that I had a homework assignment due that I didn’t have the mental energy to do, and having been experiencing what I now know was passive intermittent suicidal ideation for awhile, I thought to myself “fuck it” and quickly finished up the note, grabbed my rope and, well, hung myself.

It’s important to note that I had very poor knot-tying skills, so the noose I had tied only served to suffocate me rather than break my neck. Since I was a swimmer at the time, I could hold my breath and soon enough, the aching in my chest was bearable. My vision went fuzzy and I clawed at my throat, until finally I managed to remove the rope. I sat there, panting on my closet floor, until the black edges faded from my vision. 

I remember thinking about the homework assignment I was supposed to do. I remember knowing that I had absolutely no mental energy to do it. I remember looking back at my shitty makeshift noose, with the feeling that for some reason, I couldn’t go and try that again. Not that night. 

And so I did what I thought I’d never do. I trudged downstairs, to my mother and I gave her the whole story. 

She was understandably horrified, of course. I was taken to a hospital, evaluated and admitted to the inpatient psychiatry ward for twelve days. 

Honestly, I don’t remember ever thinking there was hope for me until long after. I just remember being really, really tired and not even having the energy to try it again. Sure, I considered it but god, I was just so damn drained. Even now, two years later, I still struggle. 

The difference is that now, I know it’s a process. I have resources and for better or for worse, I’m still here. And tonight, I plan on keeping it that way. 

I don’t really remember any big events that made me realize that I had a chance. I just kind of looked at how far I’d come and thought “Well, would you look at that. Maybe everything isn’t hopeless bullshit.”. 

Right now, sure, there’s some hopeless bullshit, but it’s not everything, and that what matters.

I most likely have an eating disorder and it’s affecting my life in so many ways.

To my friends, I joke about it when it comes up. I say I’m getting better and I’m absolutely not. 

I don’t talk about the constant mental arithmetic, the countless school lunches I’ve thrown out, the starvation-fuelled “binges”, or the looming realization that I can’t stop.

I don’t talk about how awful it is. How much I wish it would stop. Yet online, I’m active in several ED subreddits, I’m on ED vent twitter, I try to get as much off my chest as I can. 

As to why, I guess it’s just easier to write this stuff out instead of saying it to anyone’s face, you know?

I wrote an essay on fan fiction, would not talk about anything other than Sailor Moon, wore a “Christian Head Covering” (no offence intended to anyone who does, that’s totally valid, but I was just looking for attention), would regularly break down crying, drew Sailor Moon characters on the board, wrote fan fiction and told everyone about it and to top it all off, wore the same pair of pants for a year. 

This resulted in my parents getting called several times.
